title: Evening markets: Europe firmer, US opens higher before Meta and Tesla results; oil eases on Iran talk
dek: Brent slipped back from $111 after Iran's foreign minister signalled openness to diplomacy; gold held near $4,140.
body: Global markets were calmer on Wednesday evening (IST). European shares were mostly firmer after two days of losses, led by technology, property and banks, according to Newsquawk's market wrap at 7:50 pm IST (14:20 UTC). Spectacles maker EssilorLuxottica jumped 14.3% on strong sales, while French retailer Carrefour fell 14% after cutting its outlook.

In the US, stocks opened higher with the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 supported by results from Super Micro and news around SpaceX. The big events come after the US close: Meta and Tesla report quarterly results, which can move tech shares worldwide, including Indian IT stocks, on Thursday morning.

Oil turned lower. Brent traded between $107.68 and $111.32 and was near the bottom of that range, and WTI fell from $100.40 to about $96.92, after Iran's foreign minister wrote that Iran was willing to pursue diplomacy while warning it would defend itself. Spot gold held in a $4,106–4,142 range and the dollar index was steady near 101.7.
Key takeaway: if oil keeps easing from $110, that helps India's rupee and inflation outlook; Meta and Tesla results tonight will set the mood for tech stocks tomorrow.
globalImpact: Signs of diplomacy around Iran cooled oil, the biggest worry for markets this week, while US tech results are the next test for the AI-driven rally.
indiaImpact: Lower oil is good news for India's import bill, the rupee and oil-using sectors; US tech results feed into Indian IT shares, which rallied 2.9% today.
